title: Zombie Apocalypse: Trapped In an Airport Hotel For 100 Days
bildstil: Gammal motor (ägarbeslut 24/11 17:55: gammal stil tills kanalens bibliotek finns). Regeln bär bildspråket: ljusa, varma hotellmiljöer där de döda står stilla som statyer; mörka scener alltid med ficklampskägla/lykta/nödbelysning så att allt syns. Zombier = mörka silhuetter med lysande ögon; 'frozen': true = stillastående mitt i steget.
publicering: L1 18:00 Last Shift 26/11 (SATSNING_30D). Fristående Full Story – inte en del av Supercenter-serien (Part 1 väntar på bilder, 16 av 46 enligt KLICK_2026-11-26; Part 2 aldrig före Part 1).
zombieregel: De stelnar i ljus och går i mörker (they freeze in the light, they walk in the dark). Tidigare regler: värme, rörelse, vind, ljus (dras mot), ljud, lukt, trycker-aldrig-drar – denna är ny: ljus är skydd, inte lockbete.

thumb.klickfraga: En upplyst hotellobby full av döda som står stilla mitt i steget en meter från receptionisten med handen på ljusbrytaren – och regeln 'KEEP IT LIT': vad händer i sekunden lampan slocknar?
thumb.hot_i_bild: En rad döda (mörka silhuetter, lysande ögon) frusna mitt i steget under en ljuskrona, den närmaste med handen utsträckt mot disken – fyller vänstra 60 % av bilden; hjälten stor till höger bakom disken, handen på strömbrytaren.
thumb.skiljer_sig: Förra LS-miniatyren (QZquCvLDhss) var A 'THEY ONLY PUSH' vid en fängelsegrind i dagsljus och nu B split 'DAY 1 / DAY 100'. Nu: inomhus, varmt guldljus från ljuskronor, hotet står STILLA nära hjälten (LS_STANDARD 1: 'det läskiga är att de STÅR där') och en strömbrytare som insats – ny plats, ny färg (guld/vinrött mot gråblått), ny komposition (hotet diagonalt mot hjälten i stället för en mur).
thumb.jamfor_not: SKISSARK: egna layoutskisser A/B/C (PIL) i 168×94 bredvid två vinnare ur media-repots thumbs/ (3pkkFlH7-pU One Year Inside, 92UJj21YqM8 Dash). Render-körningen gör det riktiga arket med jamfor.py A B C -- 3pkkFlH7-pU 92UJj21YqM8 9LVdlATk5Zw -o chk/jamfor-ls26.png och byter sökvägen.
thumb.forsta_scen_matchar: Scen 1 (0:00–0:07) är miniatyrens värld i rörelse: samma lobby med ljuskronor och svängdörr, samma hjälte (vinröd kavaj, nyckelkort) bakom disken med skräckuttryck, de döda väller in (zombies_in lunge, shake 0.5, sfx thud); scen 2 (0:07) visar exakt miniatyr A: de stelnar mitt i steget under ljuset.

variants.scene: Varm, ljus lobby (guld/beige, vinröd matta), svängdörr i bakgrunden, ljuskronor tända. Hjälten huvud+överkropp ≈ 50 % av höjden, terror-min, handen på en stor strömbrytare med etikett 'LOBBY'. 'KEEP IT LIT' vit med svart kant ≥ 20 % av höjden. Rekommenderas.

thumb.note: Inga frågor i bild (LS_STANDARD 0 – fråge-miniatyrerna förlorade varje test 0,5–1,8 %; ersätter den äldre ordern 15/11 om en frågevariant). Inga varumärken, inga hotellkedjor, inga flygbolagslogotyper. Ingen text upprepar titeln.

forbattring.forra_videon: QZquCvLDhss 'Trapped In a Prison For 100 Days (Zombie Survival Story)' (25/11 18:00)
forbattring.matt_forra: KLICK_2026-11-26: 317 exponeringar på 16 h, 4 visningar, 1,0 % CTR, snittvisning 0:54; 100 % föreslagna videor (bredvid 'Lockdown: The Full Story'). Miniatyr A 'THEY ONLY PUSH' → B 'DAY 1 / DAY 100' bytt 10:21.
forbattring.problem: 1,0 % CTR: regeln 'THEY ONLY PUSH' måste läsas och förstås (abstrakt), och fängelsegården i dagsljus såg tom och grå ut i 168×94. Snittvisning 0:54 trots krok – tittaren fick inget visuellt löfte om vad som är farligt i varje scen. Titeln innehöll inte nischens starkaste startord.
forbattring.andring: 1) Titeln börjar med sökförslaget 'zombie apocalypse trapped in an airport hotel' (YouTube-förslag 26/11) + '100 Days' ur Full Story-mallen. 2) En regel som syns utan att läsas: ljus = de står stilla, mörker = de går – varje scen visar om lampan är tänd, så faran syns i bilden (inte bara i rösten). 3) Miniatyr A: varmt guldljus inomhus med hotet en meter från hjälten och en strömbrytare – ljusare och mer kontrast än fängelsegården. 4) 30 faktaskyltar (snitt var 19:e s) om saker tittaren har hemma eller på hotell (räkna dörrarna, kylskåpets 4 timmar, ficklampa i stället för ljus, rörelsesensorer, varmvattenberedaren). 5) En gåta som löses med en verklig mekanism (rörelsesensorerna släcker ljuset när de döda står stilla).
forbattring.forvantat: CTR ≥ 2,5 % efter 300 exp (mot 1,0 % för fängelset); ≥ 55 % kvar vid 0:30 och ≥ 35 % vid 2:00; snittvisning ≥ 2:30; söktrafik på 'zombie apocalypse trapped in'.
forbattring.referens: One Year Inside 'Trapped In Walmart After Closing 1 Year (Full Story)' (3pkkFlH7-pU) – 4 022 822 visningar (månad, Action 23/11 09:25 UTC), 48,8 min; och Dash 'Surviving 100 Days in a ZOMBIE OUTBREAK' (92UJj21YqM8) – 378 189 (vecka), 16,2 min.
forbattring.vi_slår_den_med: Samma 'Trapped In … For 100 Days'-löfte på 10 min i stället för 49: en regel man ser i varje bild (lampan tänd = säkert), en verklig mekanism som vänder regeln mot oss (rörelsesensorer – lösningen på gåtan), 30 verkliga regler på skärmen som tittaren kan använda på nästa hotell (USFA, CDC, DOE, FAA, FMCSA, BLS), människor i mitten (flygbesättningen dag 52) och ett callback-slut där tre planterade saker betalar sig: dörräkningen, isen från dag 9 och de 'statyer' som till slut står frusna i banljuset.
forbattring.trend: TREND_2026-11-26.md (Last Shift): NYTT sökförslag 26/11 under 'zombie apocalypse trapped in' → 'zombie apocalypse trapped in an airport hotel' (också: …in school, grocery store, a bunker, costco, a hospital, inside the airport). Mallen 'Trapped In … For [1 Year/100 Days] (Full Story)' – 'Trapped In Walmart After Closing 1 Year (Full Story)' – One Year Inside – 4 022 822 (månad); 'Surviving 100 Days in a ZOMBIE OUTBREAK' – Dash – 378 189 (vecka) (visningssiffror: Action 23/11 09:25 UTC – inga nyare finns). seo.sokfras = 'zombie apocalypse trapped in an airport hotel'.

experiment.variable: titel som börjar med ett sökförslag ordagrant ('Zombie Apocalypse: Trapped In an Airport Hotel') + en regel som syns i bilden (ljus/mörker)
experiment.variant: A 'KEEP IT LIT'; B split DAY 1 | DAY 100 om CTR < 2 % efter 300 exp; C '3:02 AM' om B också faller
experiment.hypothesis: En regel man ser utan att läsa (stillastående döda i ljus) ger högre CTR och 0:30-andel än en regel man måste förstå ('THEY ONLY PUSH', 1,0 %)
experiment.metric: Studio: CTR 2 h/48 h, trafikkälla YouTube-sök, 0:30-andel, snittvisning

Åtta skyltar visas bara i bild (USFA brandlarm/utrymningsplan/fire-safe list, CDC CO-detektor, FAA gult 2 000 ft och rött 1 000 ft, BLS ORS 25,1 % paus, regelskylten).

notes.research: GitHub Action ej körbar (gh-token ogiltig, GitHub-kopplingen 403 på trends.txt – 4:e dagen), vidIQ ej använd (3 krediter), YouTube/i.ytimg blockerade. Sökförslag 26/11 via suggestqueries (web-fetch). Fakta: 9 källor öppnade 26/11 via web-fetch (seo.sources) – varje siffra/regel på skyltarna står ordagrant på sidorna. USDA FSIS-sidan gick inte att öppna; kyl/frys-siffrorna kommer från CDC. BLS-lönen är May 2023 (sidan senast ändrad 3 april 2024).
notes.fiktion: Hotellet (9 våningar, 214 rum), 143 gäster/147 personer, 40 döda i lobbyn, 03:14-strömavbrottet, våning 7 och 03:02, 6 dagar diesel, override-brytaren, 60 lyktor, skytteln med 24 platser, 7 turer, två jetplan med 76 platser, 400 döda, Priya, Walt (11 år), kapten Ines Moreau och kabinpersonalen är berättelsens fiktion. Att flygfältets ljus har egen reservkraft är fiktion i berättelsen (ingen skylt). Inga verkliga hotell, flygplatser, flygbolag eller personer.

scenes.say: 11:52 PM. 143 people are asleep upstairs when the dead push through the revolving door.
Under the bright chandeliers, every one of them stops in mid-step.
They freeze in the light, and they walk in the dark.

visual.sign: THEY FREEZE IN THE LIGHT · THEY WALK IN THE DARK

scenes.say: Every trick that keeps you alive here is real and works at home.
For 100 days, 147 people live in an airport hotel that can never go dark.
On day 100, the only way out is a dark garage and a runway of colored lights.
Tonight you run the front desk alone, with 214 rooms, one master key card and a brass bell.
About 263,800 people work as hotel desk clerks in this country, at a median $14.80 an hour.

visual.sign: 263,800 HOTEL DESK CLERKS · MEDIAN $14.80 AN HOUR (BLS, MAY 2023)

scenes.say: They spend about 75 percent of the workday on their feet, and tonight you never sit down.

visual.sign: 75.1% OF THE WORKDAY STANDING (BLS ORS, 2025)

scenes.say: First problem. Forty of the dead stand frozen between your desk and the only elevators.
Priya Nair, the night housekeeping lead, slips out of the laundry room with a stack of towels.

visual.sign: FIND THE FIRE ALARMS ON YOUR FLOOR (USFA)

scenes.say: Lights on, eyes open, she whispers, because the second a bulb dies, they start walking again.
A lamp by the bar flickers for a single second, and three of them take a long step toward you.
You hit every switch on the panel behind the desk, and the lobby blazes like a showroom.

visual.sign: READ THE EVACUATION PLAN CAREFULLY (USFA)

scenes.say: Then you and Priya walk the long way around them to the stairs, counting every door you pass.
Fire officials tell hotel guests to count the doors to the exits, in case it ever goes dark.

visual.sign: COUNT THE DOORS BETWEEN YOUR ROOM AND THE EXITS (USFA)

scenes.say: They also say find the two closest exits, so you check both stairwells on all nine floors.

visual.sign: FIND THE 2 CLOSEST EXITS FROM YOUR ROOM (USFA)

scenes.say: Day 2. Second problem. 143 guests wake up, and every one of them wants to know what is happening.
All the phone lines at the desk light up at once, and you answer them in the order they ring.

visual.sign: DESK CLERKS: VERBAL INTERACTION CONSTANTLY FOR 82.2% (BLS ORS)

scenes.say: You tell every room the same three things: keep the lights on, keep the door shut, and stay upstairs.

visual.sign: FIRE-SAFE LIST: SMOKE ALARM + SPRINKLERS IN EACH ROOM, 4+ STORIES (USFA)

scenes.say: The man in room 512 doesn't listen, walks down to the garage for his rental car, and sprints back gray.
The garage lights died on night 1, and down there in the dark, they never stop walking.
Day 6. Third problem. At 3:14 AM the city grid fails, and the entire hotel goes black.
In the dark, forty bodies in the lobby start moving at once, and they are walking toward the desk.
The battery emergency lights snap on over the exits, and the whole lobby freezes three feet from you.
Upstairs, guests light candles, and the CDC says use battery flashlights and lanterns instead, to cut fire risk.

visual.sign: USE FLASHLIGHTS AND LANTERNS, NOT CANDLES (CDC)

scenes.say: Never leave a burning candle unattended, the CDC adds, and the smoke alarm in 309 is already screaming.

visual.sign: NEVER LEAVE A BURNING CANDLE UNATTENDED (CDC)

scenes.say: Priya counts six doors in the dark with one hand on the wall, and blows the candle out.
Every year there are about 3,900 hotel and motel fires in this country, and cooking is the leading cause.

visual.sign: ≈ 3,900 HOTEL AND MOTEL FIRES A YEAR · COOKING IS THE LEADING CAUSE (USFA)

scenes.say: Walt Okafor, the airport shuttle driver, drags the backup generator out onto the loading dock.
The CDC rule: no generator in a garage or basement, and a cord more than 20 feet long.

visual.sign: NEVER INSIDE A HOME, BASEMENT OR GARAGE · CORD OVER 20 FT (CDC)

scenes.say: The engine coughs twice and catches, the chandeliers glow, and the dead stand still in mid-stride.
Day 9. Fourth problem. The breakfast kitchen has two walk-in coolers and one tired generator.
Walt does the math: the generator runs the hallway lights or the coolers, never both.
The CDC says a closed refrigerator keeps food safe for up to 4 hours without power.

visual.sign: FRIDGE: SAFE UP TO 4 HOURS WITHOUT POWER IF YOU DON'T OPEN IT (CDC)

scenes.say: A full freezer holds for 48 hours, a half-full one for only 24, as long as nobody opens the door.

visual.sign: FULL FREEZER 48 HOURS · HALF-FULL 24 (CDC)

scenes.say: So you fill the freezer to the ceiling with every bag of ice from nine floors of ice machines.
Food with ice crystals left can be cooked or refrozen safely, so Walt fries everything that's thawing.

visual.sign: ICE CRYSTALS LEFT? SAFE TO COOK OR REFREEZE (CDC)

scenes.say: At midnight 147 people eat waffles under every light in the hotel, and room 512 asks for seconds.
Day 20. Fifth problem. Every night around 3 AM, the hallway lights on floor 7 go out by themselves.
Nobody touches a switch, but the corridor goes black, and something drags its feet past room 714.
Then the lights come back on, the footsteps stop, and the guests in 714 stop sleeping at all.
Priya checks the breakers twice, and there is nothing wrong with the wiring or a single bulb.

visual.sign: WITH A GENERATOR, USE A BATTERY-POWERED CO DETECTOR (CDC)

scenes.say: On day 22 you sit at the dark end of floor 7 with a flashlight in your lap and wait.
At 3:02 the lights cut out, a shape starts walking, and the moment it moves, the lights click back on.
They are motion sensors. The hotel saves power by switching hallway lights off when nothing moves.
The Department of Energy says motion sensors turn lights on when they detect motion and off a short while later.

visual.sign: MOTION SENSORS: LIGHTS ON WITH MOTION, OFF A SHORT WHILE LATER (ENERGY.GOV)

scenes.say: The dead freeze, so the sensor thinks the hall is empty, the lights die, and they start walking again.

visual.board_inset: FREEZE → NO MOTION → LIGHTS OFF → WALK

scenes.say: Infrared sensors detect heat and motion, and a body that has gone cold and still gives them neither.

visual.sign: INFRARED SENSORS DETECT HEAT AND MOTION · ULTRASONIC DETECT SOUND (ENERGY.GOV)

scenes.say: Walt finds the override in the electrical room and locks every hallway light on, for good.
Room 714 opens its door for the first time in two weeks, and the hall is a statue garden.
Day 34. Sixth problem. The taps sputter, and the airport water plant goes quiet for good.
The CDC lists water you already have: the water heater tank, and the tank behind each toilet, not the bowl.

visual.sign: WATER HEATER TANK · TOILET TANK, NOT THE BOWL (CDC)

scenes.say: The hotel has 214 toilet tanks and two giant water heaters in a basement that is pitch dark.
Priya walks down with a lantern in each hand, and every shape between her and the tanks locks in place.
Melted ice from clean water counts too, and your freezer is still packed with nine floors of ice.

visual.sign: MELTED ICE CUBES MADE WITH CLEAN WATER (CDC)

scenes.say: Day 52. Seventh problem. Landing lights sweep across the lobby windows in the middle of the night.
Captain Ines Moreau and two flight attendants cross the dark parking lot, and the dead walk with them.
You swing the luggage cart floodlight toward the lot, and every body behind them freezes in the beam.
They are shaking after hours on the cold airfield, and the CDC says below 95°F, get medical attention.

visual.sign: BODY TEMPERATURE BELOW 95°F: GET MEDICAL ATTENTION (CDC)

scenes.say: Ines says two regional jets sit fueled at the gates, 76 seats each, two miles across the dark field.

visual.sign: INSTRUMENT RUNWAYS: EDGE LIGHTS TURN YELLOW IN THE LAST 2,000 FT (FAA AIM)

scenes.say: 152 seats for 147 people, and for the first time in 52 days, the desk bell rings for good news.
Day 71. Eighth problem. Walt taps the generator gauge, and there are 6 days of diesel left.
When that engine stops, every light in the building dies with it, and 147 people stand in the dark.
So the plan becomes the jets, and the jets need a lit path from the hotel all the way to the gates.
From the roof the field still glows: runway edge lights shine white, taxiway edge lights shine blue.

visual.sign: RUNWAY EDGE LIGHTS: WHITE · TAXIWAY EDGE LIGHTS: BLUE (FAA AIM 2-1)

scenes.say: Ines draws it with salt shakers: blue marks the edges, and steady green marks the taxiway middle.

visual.sign: TAXIWAY CENTERLINE LIGHTS ARE STEADY GREEN (FAA AIM)

scenes.say: The field lights still burn, but between the hotel and that blue glow sits a garage with no power.
Day 88. Ninth problem. The garage is three levels of pure dark, and the only shuttle is parked inside.
Walt has driven it for 11 years, and any bus built for 16 or more passengers, driver included, is a commercial vehicle.

visual.sign: DESIGNED FOR 16+ PASSENGERS INCLUDING THE DRIVER = COMMERCIAL MOTOR VEHICLE (FMCSA)

scenes.say: The rule counts seats, not standing room, and this one has 24, so it's 7 trips for 147 people.

visual.sign: 'DESIGNED TO TRANSPORT' = DESIGNATED SEATS, NOT STANDING ROOM (FMCSA)

scenes.say: You and Priya hang 60 battery lanterns from the garage pillars, one every few steps.
Every lantern pins a body beneath it, and the garage turns into a museum of gray statues.
Day 100. The last problem. Seven shuttle trips through the garage before the diesel runs dry.
Trip after trip the shuttle rolls past frozen shapes, and Priya counts every head at the lobby door.

visual.sign: ONLY 25.1% OF DESK CLERKS CAN PAUSE FOR AN UNSCHEDULED BREAK (BLS ORS)

scenes.say: On trip 6, one lantern battery dies on level 2, and the dark spreads across three pillars.
Three of them lunge at the bus, Walt flicks on the high beams, and they freeze with their arms in the air.
Lights on, eyes open, Priya says, and swaps the battery with both hands shaking.
On the field, the shuttle keeps blue lights on both sides and the green line under its wheels.

visual.sign: RUNWAY CENTERLINE: RED AND WHITE, THEN ALL RED IN THE LAST 1,000 FT (FAA AIM)

scenes.say: The end lights show red toward a departing plane and green toward a plane coming in to land.

visual.sign: RUNWAY END LIGHTS: RED TO DEPARTING AIRCRAFT · GREEN TO LANDING AIRCRAFT (FAA AIM)

scenes.say: Ines takes off first, Walt's last trip fills the second jet, and Priya's count stops at 147.
Below the wings, 400 of the dead stand frozen in the runway lights, and not one of them takes a step.
Behind you, the hotel still glows on its last hour of diesel, every hallway light locked on.
Would you have opened the garage on day 88? Tell me in the comments, and count the doors to your nearest exit tonight.

visual.sub: COUNT THE DOORS TO YOUR EXIT

seo.hook: Zombie apocalypse, trapped in an airport hotel for 100 days: the dead freeze in the light and walk in the dark – and the hotel's own motion sensors keep switching the lights off. Every trick that keeps 147 people alive is real.
seo.summary: A zombie survival story told day by day from the front desk of an airport hotel: 100 days, 143 guests, a night auditor, a housekeeping lead and a shuttle driver. The dead in this story freeze the moment light touches them and walk again the second it goes dark, so every bulb in the building becomes a wall. You count the doors to the stairwells the way the U.S. Fire Administration tells hotel guests to, swap candles for flashlights before room 309 catches fire, move the generator outside with a cord over 20 feet, race the 4-hour fridge clock and the 48-hour freezer clock with nine floors of ice machines, find out why the hallway lights on floor 7 keep going out at 3 AM, drink from the water heaters and toilet tanks like the CDC suggests, and on day 100 drive 147 people through a pitch-black parking garage to two jets waiting under blue taxiway lights. Every rule and number on screen is real – BLS, U.S. Fire Administration, CDC, Department of Energy, FAA and FMCSA – and the outbreak is fiction.

U.S. Fire Administration – Hotel and vacation rental fire safety (count the doors between your room and the exits; find the 2 closest exits; fire alarms; evacuation plan; ≈3,900 hotel and motel fires a year, cooking leading cause; hard-wired smoke alarm + sprinklers in each room for 4+ stories)

CDC – What to Do to Protect Yourself During a Power Outage (flashlights and lanterns rather than candles; never a generator in a home, basement or garage; cord more than 20 feet; battery CO detector; fridge up to 4 hours; full freezer 48 h, half-full 24 h; refreeze with ice crystals; below 95°F get medical attention)
CDC – Proper Use of Candles During a Power Outage (never leave a burning candle unattended)
CDC – How to Find Clean Water in an Emergency (water heater tank; toilet tank, not the bowl; melted ice cubes made with uncontaminated water)
U.S. Department of Energy – Lighting controls (motion sensors turn lights on with motion and off a short while later; infrared sensors detect heat and motion, ultrasonic detect sound)

FAA Aeronautical Information Manual 2-1 – Airport lighting aids (runway edge white, yellow last 2,000 ft on instrument runways; taxiway edge blue; taxiway centerline steady green; runway end red/green; centerline all red last 1,000 ft)
FMCSA – CMV 'designed to transport' 16 or more passengers including the driver (designated seats only, not standing room)

seo.disclaimer: The outbreak, the hotel and every person in it are fiction; the safety rules and numbers on screen are real. Not professional safety advice – follow official guidance in a real emergency.
